Subject: QBR: BlueSigma health dashboard & renewal risk register — exec flags & asks

Team — kicking off prep for the BlueSigma QBR next week. Attached is the latest health workbook (v3) and the mutual action plan draft. High level summary first, then asks for exec review: 

Snapshot (last 30 days)
- Production inference latency: 95th percentile 210ms (target 200ms) — transient spikes during nightly batch.
- Token cost trend: +6% MoM due to increased prompt length on search reranker route.
- Uptime: 99.92% (incidents: 1 partial outage, mitigated with fallback to quantized model)
- Customer sentiment: CS survey score 7.8/10, call notes show concern around rate limits during peak ETL windows.

Renewal risk register (top lines)
1) Rate-limit pressure on reranker route -> product reliability perception (risk: Medium-High).
2) Procurement delay for multi-year contract; legal wants a data residency addendum (risk: Medium).
3) Pricing pushback due to rising token spend (risk: Medium).

Exec attention items (I want 2 bullets we can surface to the exec during QBR):
- Proposal: 30-day targeted burst capacity pilot (Dedicated reserved lanes) to demonstrate stability for peak ETL runs — requires Ops capacity approval and a $12k test credit.
- Contract ask: approve a one-off concession on overage rates while we finalize a quantization rollout (finance approval for a 10% credit cap).

Please review the attached workbook tabs: "Health Dashboard", "Risk Register", "Evals & Prompts", "MAP (v1)". Grace — can you update the risk register with quantized rollout ETA and Ops feasibility by EOD? Jordan — can you draft the two-line exec framing for the QBR deck? Karthik — flag any product roadmap commitments that would affect the ETA.

Attachments: BlueSigma_QBR_health_workbook_v3.xlsx (workbook, 4 tabs), BSIG_mutual_action_plan_2027-08.docx (07/12 MAP draft)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick pass from ops/product.

Thanks for the workbook. Notes: 
- Quantized rollout ETA: internal staging by 2027-09-10, can start customer pilot 2027-09-20 if we lock a small reserved pool now.
- Ops capacity: we can provision a 2-week burst lane this quarter but need written approval; cost estimate ~ $12,000 as you noted.
- Root cause for latency spikes: KV cache invalidation during nightly prompt refresh; fix requires a small runtime change that is low-risk but needs a canary (2–3% requests).

I'll update the Risk Register tab with ETA fields and a mitigations column. Also adding a short note about the canary timeline.

Action items I own: 
1) Update risk register (ETA: EOD 23 Aug).
2) Draft scope for ops pilot and cost breakdown (ETA: 24 Aug 10:00 PT).

Marissa / team — thanks for the clear summary and for pulling the workbook together. A few notes from our side before the QBR: 

- Procurement: our legal lead (cc'd) needs the data residency addendum language and a short note on audit logging retention (we currently store logs for 90 days; they want 180 for one dataset). Is that feasible?
- Cost: we are sensitive to any permanent price increases. The pilot approach for burst capacity sounds fine as a short-term fix; we'll want a clear stop-gap credit so our finance team can approve the pilot quickly.
- Goals for QBR: please surface a clear timeline for (a) quantized pilot, (b) canary for runtime fix, and (c) precise cost delta for burst lane (so we can take to procurement).

I'll loop in our finance/legal and confirm availability for the QBR on Tue 31 Aug 10:00 PT — does that work for you?

Thanks,
